# Pesher Nahum Column 1 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

This log records all lines in Pesher Nahum Column 1 where the three translators diverged, along with SOPHIA's resolution.

---

## 1:4 — "yigga'ar" — rendering of God's rebuke of the sea

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "He rebukes the sea and-dries-it-up" | Hyphenated construct preserving Hebrew conjunctions |
| LOGOS | "He rebukes the sea and dries it up" | Standard formal English |
| PNEUMA | "He rebukes the sea and dries it up; He makes all the rivers run dry" | "run dry" more vivid than "desolate" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS phrasing with "desolate" for rivers (EMET/LOGOS). PNEUMA's "run dry" loses the desolation imagery of the Hebrew charev.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 1:5 — "pishro" — the pesher formula

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Its pesher:" | Preserves Hebrew technical term with possessive |
| LOGOS | "Its pesher:" | Same as EMET |
| PNEUMA | "The meaning of this:" | Translates pesher into natural English |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "Its pesher:" — the term pesher is a technical genre designation that should remain untranslated throughout DSS texts.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 1:6 — "le-hashmidam" — "to destroy them"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "to-destroy-them from-upon the face-of" | Hyphenated literal with me'al preserved |
| LOGOS | "to destroy them from the face of" | Standard formal rendering |
| PNEUMA | "wipe them from the face of" | "wipe" conveys totality of destruction |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "to destroy them from the face of." EMET's hyphenation is unnecessarily mechanical; PNEUMA's "wipe" imports connotations not in the Hebrew shamad.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 1:7 — "yitmogegu" — rendering of hills melting

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the hills melt" | Standard literal rendering of mug |
| LOGOS | "the hills melt" | Same as EMET |
| PNEUMA | "the hills dissolve" | "dissolve" captures the totality of the image |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "melt" (EMET/LOGOS). "Melt" is the standard equivalent for Hebrew mug in theophanic contexts and preserves the fire-imagery coherence of the passage.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 1:7 — "nasa'ah" — the earth's response

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the earth heaves before-Him" | "heaves" for nasa' in earthquake context |
| LOGOS | "the earth heaves before Him" | Same verb choice |
| PNEUMA | "the earth convulses before Him" | "convulses" more dramatic and accessible |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "heaves" (EMET/LOGOS). The Hebrew nasa' means "to lift up"; "heaves" captures the upward motion accurately. "Convulses" overstates.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 1:10 — "bechirey El" — the chosen of God

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the chosen-ones of-God" | Hyphenated construct |
| LOGOS | "the chosen ones of God" | Standard formal |
| PNEUMA | "God's chosen people" | Possessive form; adds "people" for clarity |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "the chosen ones of God." PNEUMA's addition of "people" is interpretive — the Hebrew says bechirey, "chosen ones," without specifying further.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 1:10 — "'edah" — congregation vs. community

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "his congregation" | 'edah as "congregation" |
| LOGOS | "his congregation" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "his community" | More accessible modern term |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "congregation" (EMET/LOGOS). 'Edah is a technical term for the Qumran assembly and "congregation" is the established scholarly equivalent.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 1:11 — "za'mo" — "His indignation" vs. "His fury"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "His indignation" | Standard rendering of za'am |
| LOGOS | "His indignation" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "His fury" | Simpler, more direct |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Retained "His indignation" (EMET/LOGOS). Za'am specifically denotes indignation/denunciation, distinct from the more general chemah ("fury/anger") that appears later in the same verse.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of EMET/LOGOS.

---

## 1:11 — "nitteku" — rocks broken

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the rocks are-broken-asunder by-Him" | Hyphenated compound for nitteku |
| LOGOS | "the rocks are broken asunder by Him" | Standard formal |
| PNEUMA | "the very rocks shatter before Him" | "shatter" more vivid; "very" adds emphasis |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS "the rocks are broken asunder by Him." "Broken asunder" preserves the Niphal passive of natak. PNEUMA's "shatter" changes the voice and "very" is an addition.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

**Total disagreements for Column 1:** 9
